args.summary:
This session was a bronze-age save as Israel, at war with Pontus.

**What worked**
- Buying a build with gold was clear: there is a confirm step and the farm finished right away.
- The era goal cards are engaging.
- The Auto siege flow is quick.

**Main problems**
1. **Naval is a dead end.** I scrolled the whole Units list in Samaria, Megiddo and Hazor and found no ship in any of them. Nothing on screen tells me which cities count as coastal or which tech unlocks ships, so I could not test naval at all.
2. **Siege odds look broken.** Jerusalem had the same 3,000 militia both turns. Against 33,340 attackers the preview said "Auto holds 100%"; the next turn, against fewer attackers (30,220), it said "Auto holds 0%, Hopeless".
3. **No result screen after an Auto fight.** Fight on Auto drops me straight back on the map without saying what happened.
4. **Rebuilding an army is far too slow.** One Composite Archers regiment takes about 24 turns in a pop-3 city, and buying it costs about 500 g

args.summary: Session from turn 116 to 126 at war with Akkad. Good: the threat alerts (Defend, then Send an army) lead well into the city Defense tab. Buying with gold is clear and the confirm box explains the 40% price rise. Turns pass quickly with autosave, and the governor prompts are tidy. Problems: the Best site preview said Berenice but the city was founded as Gezer. A new city stays an Outpost that can't build anything for 29 turns, and nothing warned me. After I confirmed a March order, the camera jumped to an unrelated region. A 5-turn march is slow when the enemy is 2 tiles away. Shechem is under siege now, the advisor suggests an Earthwork Ditch, and the bought archers held. The war pacing feels tense and fun. The city and build panels are dense but usable on a phone.

args.summary: Gunpowder session, turns 331 to 335. I looked at every checklist area. What worked: the World Congress vote panel is clear and the tally updates when you vote. Signing a pact with Nok for gold was easy. The era goal card is readable, and it was nice that the Science goal (8 of 9) is close to done. The buy confirm explains the price clearly. Keeping the trading post for +2000 gold felt rewarding. Problems: buy prices are very high next to income. A Bank cost 2324g while I made about +300 a turn, so you can only buy after a windfall. The queue dropdown arrow flipped but no list opened. The Harbor showed 149/144 production but still said 6 turns. The Frigate's buy price changed from 1122 to 929 between turns and nothing said why. The governor and restless-city prompts pile up on the left side of the map. Overall the pacing is decent and the menus are fairly quick. Fun about 3 to 4 out of 5.

args.summary: Modern-age session from turn 472 to 480. City builds, the advisor fill and buying with gold all work well, and the buy confirm is clear. The World Congress vote and paid peace with Saba were quick and clean, and event cards read well. Main problem: enemy strength numbers for Zafar were not consistent. The scout guessed 12k to 18k, the battle report showed 44.9k, and the march preview said 294.9k, all within two turns, so I couldn't trust any forecast. Wars feel risky without good intel. Pontus declared war near the end. Ending turns is fast and the turn pace is good. Being asked over and over to pick builds for idle cities gets tedious, but the advisor and Always buttons help.

args.text: Late game (turns 618 to 645), most turns are just End Turn with nothing to do. The only breaks are event cards that ask to trade gold for stability. I had 18 unspent ruler attribute points, and each one costs a tap. Please add a bulk spend option and more late-game goals or prompts so turns don't feel empty.

thought: I'm writing down how slow the late game feels before I wrap up.

name: done

args.summary: Late information-age session (turns 618 to 645). Things that worked: event cards (pandemic, banks, merchants, bus service) explain their trade-offs clearly, the tribute demand card was clear, autosave is reliable, and the turns themselves run fast. Problems: the late game is thin. Most turns are just End Turn. You can only spend ruler attribute points one tap at a time (I had 18 unspent), so please add a bulk spend. Gold piles up with little to spend it on. Every checklist area was looked at across the session. Overall fun 3/5, frustration low.

thought: I'm wrapping up. The game is stable, but the late game needs more goals.
